subject: Cloud Computing
title: Choosing the Right Database
description: A fast breakdown of Choosing the Right Database for builders.

hook.text: Relational, document, key-value, graph, time-series — there are dozens of database types. Which one do you need?

buildup.text: Relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL) excel at structured data with complex relationships and transactions.

discovery.text: NoSQL databases (DynamoDB, MongoDB) handle unstructured data and scale horizontally with ease.

twist.text: There's no universal best database. Teams that choose based on hype instead of requirements regret it quickly.

climax.text: Cloud managed databases remove the operational burden. You choose the engine; the provider handles backups and patches.

punchline.text: Pick the database for the problem. Not the one that's trending.

quiz.question: When are NoSQL databases a better choice than relational?
options: For unstructured data that needs to scale horizontally
For complex transactions involving many related tables
For storing financial data with strict consistency requirements

details.summary: Cloud providers offer dozens of database types including relational, document, key-value, graph, time-series, and ledger databases. The right choice depends on data structure, query patterns, consistency needs, and scale requirements rather than familiarity or trend.
details.whyItMatters: Choosing the wrong database creates performance bottlenecks and expensive migrations later. Matching the database to the workload is one of the most impactful architecture decisions.
takeaways: Match the database type to your data model and query patterns
Relational databases suit structured data with complex queries
NoSQL databases excel at specific access patterns and scale

faq.question: When should you choose a relational database?
faq.answer: Choose relational when you need complex joins, transactions across multiple tables, strong consistency, and ad-hoc querying. PostgreSQL and MySQL on managed services like RDS or Cloud SQL handle most general-purpose workloads well.

faq.question: When should you choose a NoSQL database?
faq.answer: Choose NoSQL when you have a known access pattern, need massive horizontal scale, or work with semi-structured data. DynamoDB excels at key-value lookups, MongoDB at flexible documents, and Cassandra at high write throughput across regions.
